explanation: Pointing directly at a PERSON with your index finger can come across as accusatory or confrontational in the Philippines, similar to many other cultures; the common polite alternative is 'pointing with the lips' (a slight purse of the lips toward the direction) or gesturing with an open hand. Pointing at objects or places with a finger is much more neutral and unlikely to cause offense.
local_tip: To indicate a person or a sensitive topic, purse your lips toward them instead of pointing; for objects or directions, an open hand or a regular finger-point is generally fine.
regional_note: Among younger, urbanized Filipinos, pointing with the index finger at a person is tolerated more among close friends, but it's still best avoided with elders or in formal settings.

also_check.note: Pointing with the index finger is considered impolite; an open hand or a nod toward the object/person is preferred.
Pointing at a person with the index finger is considered offensive; many Indonesians also point with the lips or thumb.
Pointing is common and generally acceptable in casual contexts, though pointing at a person can read as aggressive in formal settings.
